body: @JSwetz, a heads-up to save you a round: this one and #3880 conflict with main only in the **3D rough-finish catalog case** (`examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/rough-finish.camproj`/`.nc`, and for #3880 `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/case_3d_rough_finish.rs`). Main's #3857 (3D Pocket re-entry takes the entry) changed those goldens at 06:0x UTC. A `git merge upstream/main` and regenerating that case's golden should clear both. #3881 and #3883 conflict in `crates/app/tests/mcp_live/ui_link.rs`, likely with each other's or a merged neighbour's test. None of the four has a review yet; once they merge cleanly, reviews start right away. Thanks for taking the P3 bugs!

Addressed: The catalog conflict was resolved locally. Merged main `582981bfa` into this branch (maintainer edit, approved by the reporter). Kept main's catalog files, then regenerated `3d/rough-finish` with the PR change. No push was made. Local head `25e3e2b99d4d1e09d5f3e0bcee1573b464e32639` remains in `.claude/worktrees/fix-3869`.

Quick passed all 31 steps. Motion clippy passed. All four `pocket3d_stock_to_leave` pins passed. Removing the PR changes made three allowance pins fail; restoring them made all four pass. Stopped: heavy completed 104 steps with one failure and no stalls. `app:pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` failed. Its Linux mesh assertion expected 6,228 facets and got 5,232 before toolpath generation. The test, STEP fixture, and importer match main. No unrelated fix was made.

Upstream main moved to `3593a6123` during the gate. This local merge uses `582981bfa`. A further refresh and checks are needed.

**Needs changes before merge.** The fix is correct and safe. One process item in the PR body is missing (item 1 below). The code needs no change.

This is a SAFETY-tier review: the PR changes the posted G-code of 3D Pocket roughing.

### What looks good

- The level law is correct. The ladder probes `level_target` at `z - stock_to_leave` and keeps the `r + stock_to_leave` erosion. A model point above `z - s` is in the shadow, so the tool stays `r + s` from it in XY. A model point at or below `z - s` is at least `s` below the tool tip. The superset law stays true, because the shift is a constant.
- `pocket3d_air_split` (rotary wrap only, `rotary_offset.rs:294`) passes `0.0`, so the rotary output does not change. The decision file says this.
- The floor band change applies only when `stock_to_leave > 0`. `params.rs:110` refuses a negative allowance, so the `z - s` probe cannot move up into the model.
- The pinning tests measure the 3D distance from the tool envelope to the model on the `3d/rough-finish` case. They do this with a mesh scan and with an analytic scan. This is the "Done when" condition of #3669.
- The tests cover Waterline, OffsetRings, Adaptive, the offset shell and rest, and also a flat-top boss and a through pocket.
- `docs/decisions/3669-3d-pocket-stock-to-leave.md` is present. The new test file has its provenance line and its Gate map. `ladder.rs` gets 2 lines shorter.

### Results (locally, trial merge with upstream/main `808c540a9`)

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 31 steps, 0 failed. This includes `motion suites: pocket3d_stock_to_leave` (4 tests), `lib`, `blind_floor`, `pocket3d_hsm`, `pocket3d_troch`, `rotary_adaptive`, `rotary_zigzag_rings`, `top_z_level`, and the app suites `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `pocket3d_trochoid`, `shared_face_bodies`, `first_part_programs`.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`): 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: not run. This is a `P3` PR, so no heavy step is necessary ("Heavy lanes at review").

Extra suites run: none were necessary. The diff does not touch `testdata/` or the importers.

### Mutations (both red, then restored)

1. `ladder.rs`: probe at `z` instead of `z - axial_leave`. Result: `rough_finish_dome_and_plate_keep_axial_and_radial_allowance` fails with `mesh tool-envelope distance 0.0000 mm fell below allowance 0.5 - 0.01`.
2. `floor_levels.rs`: `in_band = z > first` (the old band). Result: two tests fail, with `missing allowance level Z 18.5` and `expected plate floor cut at Z8.5`.

### Goldens moved

`examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/rough-finish.nc` and `.camproj` (the body names this case). I compared the Z levels of the program on main and on the trial merge:

- T01 (roughing): the last level moves from Z8. (the plate top, 0 allowance) to Z8.5. At Z18 the zigzag lines no longer cross the dome apex. They stop at about R8 from the axis (sphere radius 4.58 at Z17.5, plus 3.5). I checked one helix re-entry (Z20 to Z18) by hand: it keeps 0.61 mm from the dome. The envelope scan of the pinning test covers all the moves. The smallest feed Z is 8.5.
- T02 (finishing): no change. The Z levels and the move counts are the same.
- `example_catalog` passes on the trial merge, so the recorded program agrees with the generator.

### Requested before merge

1. **New top-level test binary without a reason** (AGENTS.md "New tests join a directory suite", #3187). `crates/motion/tests/pocket3d_stock_to_leave.rs` is a new top-level test file. The PR body does not give the one-line reason that the law requires. Do one of these:
   - Add one line to the PR body that says why the file is a new top-level binary.
   - Or move the tests into an existing directory suite of `crates/motion/tests/`.

   A body edit is sufficient. The code and the head do not need to change.

### Optional, non-blocking

- The body ends with `Refs #2392`. The Pull Request Law says that the body ends with `Fixes #N`. Put `Refs #2392` above `Fixes #3669`.
- At the Z18 level, each zigzag line now splits at the dome crown. Each split adds a full retract to Z47 and a helix re-entry (T01 has 16 more retract lines). This is safe, but slow. A keep-down link around the crown can be a `P7` follow-up.
- The rotary wrap path (`pocket3d_air_split`) still applies the allowance only radially. The decision file records this. A follow-up issue can make this visible to the user.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
